description:
Advance the sign-in on the current tab: account choice, consent, filling the saved username and password, and checking the result.

Supply your assessment of the tab's current view, with what the page shows and its control references. The credential service takes the account from your sign-in context, obtains the user's consent and fills the fields without revealing them. Your sign-in context holds the account from the `account_hint` that started or followed up your work, or the one Muse chose since. The result gives the status, the account's label and anything unresolved. A result that stops short of a sign-in names the sign-in page's site.

The call waits while the user decides and resumes on its own. When the page redrew meanwhile, it finds the same fields and provider control on the page as it is then, so the user is not asked twice; a field the site cleared, such as after a CAPTCHA, is filled again under the same approval. After a site rejected a sign-in, whether to try again is your decision; say what the page shows in `previous_attempt`. The call does not enter one-time codes, which you type with `browser.act`, and it cannot switch accounts, resend a code or get around a lockout. A purchase whose outcome is still unknown does not hold the sign-in. If the page changes, call `login.advance` again with your assessment of the new observation it returns.

username_field.description: The reference of the visible, editable username, email or phone field for the current sign-in step, from controls; null when absent, read-only or disabled, including a read-only account identifier on a password-only step.

password_field.description: The reference of the visible, editable password field for the current sign-in step, from controls; null when absent, read-only or disabled.

google_button.description: The reference of the visible Google sign-in control, whatever element it is, such as a button, a link or a framed button; null when the page shows none.

apple_button.description: The reference of the visible Apple sign-in control, whatever element it is, such as a button, a link or a framed button; null when the page shows none.

amazon_button.description: The reference of the visible Amazon sign-in control, whatever element it is, such as a button, a link or a framed button; null when the page shows none.

previous_attempt.description: What the page shows about an earlier sign-in attempt: rejected when it shows one failed, such as a wrong password message, none when it shows no earlier attempt, unknown otherwise.
